touches.text: Machine: tools plus the glue that holds them together. Has an owner. Anything that calls another component, uses other tools, or owns state it must gate is a machine. Lives inside its device (cairn/devices/<device>/machines/<machine>/), or in cairn/machines/ when several devices hold one (16).
Commit often. WHY: so we never wind up with stray files or incomplete work.

Install and upgrades live here: the installer machine walks the host-seam intentions, verifies each, offers what's missing, applies, re-verifies. If xyz library needs an update, this is the component that does it. Any change to what the host is goes through here (6.6.3.1.1).

The line is using vs changing. Any device may USE the OS's services (write a file, open a socket, start or stop its own unit with systemctl). CHANGING what the host is (installing or updating systemd unit files, packages, udev rules, cron entries) goes through Recovery. Eg Cairn restarts the bus itself; putting the bus's unit file in place goes through Recovery.
It outputs only its findings. It certifies nothing, records no crossing, and posts nothing; the gate consumes its findings.

Where a tool lives: the general collection, cairn/tools/, is the default. A tool goes with its holder (cairn/devices/<d>/tools/) only when nothing else could ever use it: "if i build a tool for adjusting the farfignator on a vw golf from the 80s, and nothing else in the universe has a farfignator, then it can go with the car." If there is any chance somebody else might want it, it goes in the general collection.
